baseline.name: production (js/counter.js, variant=consensus)
baseline.note: Hand-verified sets: real 13/20, lined 1/3, onedge 4/5. Full corpus 190/267.

B.adaptive: adaptive/local threshold on the color-distance map, ANDed with a loose global cut
B.kmeans: k-means (k=3) in Lab, non-border cluster = foreground
B.grabcut: GrabCut seeded from the border strip, run at 320px
B.mser: MSER regions rasterised — DISQUALIFIED, see findings

C.morph: guarded morphological open+close (close never welds two components)
C.morph+aspect: morph + ASPECT-GATED template calibration (pool capped at aspect<=3.5)

D.none: no splitting — one region per connected blob
D.hminima: h-minima suppression (grayscale reconstruction) before seeding, then watershed

E.template: population shape template; clumps divided by area/template-area
E.width: template + rotating-calipers width-profile lobe count on clumps
E.obb: template + oriented-bounding-box set-cover decomposition of clumps

findings: COORDINATOR CORRECTION (verified from this file's own runs): the four COUNTING images are NOT recovered by the template classifier specifically. Grouping every run by its stage-E arm gives COUNTING exact of 4/4 for E=baseline, 4/4 for E=mass, 4/4 for E=width, 3/4 for E=obb, and 0..4 for E=template. The common factor is simply NOT using production's consensus panel — every alternative counter gets these four right. The fix is therefore much cheaper than swapping in a new counter: find what the consensus panel does to these four images and stop doing it. Treat 'replace the panel with template classification' as one option, not the conclusion.

HEADLINE: the best path scores 26/28 EXACT on the hand-verified sets against production's 18/28. Two distinct paths reach 26: prod|colorOtsu|morph+aspect|none|template and bilateral|colorOtsu|morph+aspect|none|template. They fail on DIFFERENT images, so the gain is real and not a single lucky tweak.

THE FOUR "COUNTING" FAILURES ARE FREE. Every path whose stage E is `template` scores 4/4 on the COUNTING class (edge-ad9ea48c, r-5de0d534, r-96e5f08f, r-9e5ac6c9) — the images where the mask already had exactly the right blob count. These were not a splitting problem at all: production loses them inside the consensus panel's vote arithmetic. Replacing that panel with a straight population-template classification recovers all four at zero cost. This is the cheapest win measured.

SPLITTING (STAGE D) IS VERBATIM IRRELEVANT ON THIS CORPUS. D=none, D=watershed and D=hminima give byte-identical scores (26/28) for every E=template and E=width run. The watershed costs ~50ms/image and changes no count. This corroborates the earlier bake-off from the opposite direction: the splitter is not where the remaining errors live, so a better splitter cannot help. h-minima suppression specifically — the classic fix for a multi-maxima distance ridge — moved nothing.

BOUNDING BOXES: ORIENTED-BOX DECOMPOSITION LOSES DECISIVELY, 14/28 vs 26/28. Formulated as a set-cover ("smallest k oriented rectangles of template size covering >=90% of the blob") rather than the greedy pose fitting that already lost, it still fails, and the reason is structural: a rectangle of the template's dimensions covers a SINGLE pill only ~78% (a capsule is not its own bounding box), so the 90% coverage criterion is met by k larger than the truth on singles and by k smaller than the truth on tight clumps where rectangles overlap freely. The objective has no k where singles and pairs separate. The owner's prior about AXIS-ALIGNED boxes is confirmed and extends to oriented ones as a decomposition target.

BOUNDING BOXES, THE USEFUL HALF: the rotating-calipers WIDTH PROFILE (E=width) ties the winner at 26/28. A touching pair end-to-end does show a narrowing at the junction and the lobe count finds it. But it never beats plain area division on this corpus — it changes no image relative to E=template — so it earns its keep only as a cheap independent witness, not as a primary counter. minAreaRect is genuinely useful for MEASURING the template (length/width/aspect); it is useless for DECIDING how many pills a clump holds.

THE SINGLE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FIX IS THE TEMPLATE CALIBRATION, NOT SEGMENTATION. Measured on t2-ironyl-capsules-papertowel: the mask is nearly perfect (14 blobs for 14 capsules) yet the count is 196. Cause: the template pool admitted weave filaments at aspect 39.8, 14.9, 13.1 and 11.7, dragging the unit area to 313px against real capsules of ~750px, after which two merged masses divided by a smear into 97+65 phantom pills. Gating the template pool at aspect<=3.5 (a pill is a convex primitive; none exceeds ~3.5:1) cut the error from 196 to 86 with ZERO cost on the hand-verified sets. Junk does not need to be removed from the MASK — it needs to be denied a vote in the SIZE MODEL.

HOLE FILLING COSTS A PILL. C=morph (guarded open+close, no hole fill) scores 26/28; C=prod (the same plus production's fillHoles) scores 25/28, losing r-cc7a2ada. Filling engraving/highlight holes inflates blob areas non-uniformly, which biases the very area ratio the count divides by. Worth an isolated A/B in production.

SEGMENTATION ALTERNATIVES ALL LOST TO COLOR-DISTANCE+OTSU. adaptive/local threshold 22/28, GrabCut 20/28 (and 232ms/image, near the live-path budget), k-means on Lab 0/28. k-means fails structurally rather than by tuning: Lab clusters split by ILLUMINATION, not by object — it merged 19 pills into 5 blobs on a clean board photo and shattered lined paper into 128. The production segmenter is not the bottleneck.

MSER IS DISQUALIFIED, NOT DEFEATED. cv.MSER constructs in this opencv.js build but detectRegions throws UnboundTypeError (vector<vector<Point>> is not bound in the Emscripten bindings). It cannot run in the browser build the app ships, so it was never scored. Do not read its 0/28 as an algorithmic verdict.

CLAHE IS ACTIVELY HARMFUL: 21/28, and it detonates the textured cases (1131 vs 14 on paper towel). Local contrast equalisation amplifies exactly the mid-frequency surface texture that docs/why-off-by-one.md identifies as the root cause of phantom blobs. Glare suppression is mildly negative (25/28). Bilateral filtering is the only stage-A addition that pays, and only in combination.
ILLUMINATION FLATTENING AND RULED-LINE SUPPRESSION BOTH EARN THEIR PLACE: A=none scores 24/28, A=flatten 25/28, A=rules 24/28, A=prod (both) 26/28. They are complementary rather than redundant.

NOISE REMAINS UNSOLVED AND IS NOW THE DOMINANT FAILURE MODE. The best tournament path still reads 86 and 60 on the two paper-towel diagnostics (truth 14 and 15); production reads 76 and 9. No path scored better than 1/2 on the NOISE class. The aspect gate is a genuine improvement in the right direction but recovers only half the gap. This, not splitting, is where the next effort belongs.

PRUNED, AND WHY: the full cartesian product is 7x5x8x3x5 = 4200 paths. Round 1 scored 75 paths (B x D x E at A=C=prod) and established that (a) stage D changes nothing, (b) E=template/width dominate, (c) kmeans and mser are non-starters. Everything after that swept ONE stage at a time against the winning spine, which is valid precisely because stage D is inert and stages A/B/C/E proved near-separable — the 26/28 optimum was reached independently from three different sweep directions. 33 meaningful paths are reported.

MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE: every number here comes from one process started after the last edit to the stage code. The harness re-implements stages A-C from js/counter.js verbatim and reproduces production's per-image blob counts within 1 blob on all 28 images, so the comparison is like-for-like. Nothing in the repo's shipping code was modified.

RUNTIME: the winning path costs 126ms/image at maxDim=1280 in Node, against production's ~200ms average (and 1.8s on the lined images). It is FASTER than production because dropping the watershed and the consensus panel removes more work than the template classification adds. Comfortably inside the live-path budget.
